question: A matrix $X$ satisfies $$2X'+\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\3&0&4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7&0&3\\1&6&-2\end{bmatrix}.$$ Determine the order and entries of $X$, and verify the result by substituting the obtained matrix into the original equation.
explanation:
Determination of $X'$

The matrices appearing with $X'$ are of order $2\times3$. Therefore, $X'$ must be of order $2\times3$, and hence $X$ is of order $3\times2$. From the given equation, $$2X'=\begin{bmatrix}7&0&3\\1&6&-2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\3&0&4\end{bmatrix}$$ $$2X'=\begin{bmatrix}6&-2&4\\-2&6&-6\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$X'=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1&2\\-1&3&-3\end{bmatrix}$$ Taking transpose on both sides, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&3\\2&-3\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

For the obtained matrix, $$X'=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1&2\\-1&3&-3\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$2X'=\begin{bmatrix}6&-2&4\\-2&6&-6\end{bmatrix}$$ Adding the given matrix, $$2X'+\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\3&0&4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7&0&3\\1&6&-2\end{bmatrix}$$ which is exactly the right-hand side of the original equation. Therefore, the required matrix is $$X=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&3\\2&-3\end{bmatrix}$$ of order $3\times2$.
